passage:
Four students started the Lunch Box Club. The rule was simple: each member had to bring one extra small dish every Friday and share it with the others.
At first, they only shared food. One brought eggs, another brought fruit, another brought noodles, and another brought vegetables.
Soon, they began sharing stories too. Each dish came from a family habit. One student's grandmother made pickles every winter. Another student's father cooked curry when he was happy.
Other classmates wanted to join, so the club made a new rule. Food had to be simple and safe, and everyone had to explain where it came from.
The Lunch Box Club became more than lunch. It became a way to taste different homes.
